phases.name: Phase 1: Freeze the contract
phases.description: Separate supplied targets from design assumptions before drawing the pipeline.

phases.name: Phase 2: Trigger and prepare data
phases.description: Accept scheduled and drift-driven requests, validate versioned inputs, and record run lineage.

phases.name: Phase 3: Train and evaluate
phases.description: Train reproducibly, compare with the incumbent, and block unqualified candidates.

phases.name: Phase 4: Release and operate safely
phases.description: Swap versions without downtime, observe production quality, and feed drift signals back into retraining.

steps.title: Start from the frozen problem brief
steps.content:
Problem: Design an Automated Model Retraining Pipeline (mlops_005). Description: Design a system that automatically retrains ML models when performance degrades or new data arrives, validates retrained models against quality gates, and deploys approved models to production. Category: MLOps - Continuous Training; domain: aiml; difficulty: Medium. The brief does not specify an estimated time.

Requirements (verbatim):
- Trigger retraining on schedule or drift detection
- Automatically collect and validate training data
- Train models with consistent configurations
- Evaluate retrained models against baselines
- Implement quality gates for deployment approval
- Roll back to previous model on validation failure
- Track all retraining events and outcomes
- Support both scheduled and event-driven retraining

Constraints (verbatim):
- Retraining completion within 4 hours
- New model must outperform current by >1%
- Zero-downtime model swap in production
- Handle data schema changes gracefully
- Maintain model lineage across retraining cycles

Hints (verbatim):
- Use CI/CD principles applied to ML (CT/CD)
- Implement shadow deployments for validation
- Use statistical significance tests for comparison
- Implement data validation with Great Expectations
- Use blue-green deployments for zero-downtime swaps
- Implement circuit breaker patterns for model rollback

Companies listed for context only: Google, Amazon, Uber, and Spotify; none mandates a vendor. The brief does not specify peak data volume, model family, comparison metric, significance level, or the 4-hour clock boundary. Treat the named targets as acceptance criteria to demonstrate, not proof of achievable performance.

steps.title: Resolve policy questions without inventing them
steps.content: Before implementation, agree what measurable metric defines the required greater-than-1% improvement (absolute or relative), the evaluation population, statistical test and confidence threshold, and whether the four-hour window starts at trigger acceptance or data availability. Define drift windows and minimum sample sizes to avoid noisy retraining. Treat the frozen brief's numeric targets as hard gates once their measurement definitions are approved; do not silently weaken them when capacity is tight.

steps.title: Give every run an immutable identity
steps.content: Create a run ID at trigger acceptance and use it as the idempotency key throughout the workflow. A run manifest should pin the dataset snapshot and schema, feature code, training code/container digest, parameters, random seeds where applicable, evaluation set, incumbent model version, and policy version. Retries resume or safely repeat the same run rather than creating an untraceable second candidate.

steps.title: Add the operator console
steps.content: The console shows schedules, drift signals, run state, gate results, and the currently serving model. Operators can inspect and approve only the policy-defined actions; the user interface is not itself a deployment gate.

component.label: ML Operations Console
component.description: Operator view for schedules, run lineage, quality results, approvals, and release state.

properties.purpose: Display retraining runs, pinned inputs, quality-gate evidence, and release or rollback status.

component.highlightReason: Makes automated retraining observable and reviewable without making the UI authoritative.

steps.title: Add the control API
steps.content: Expose authenticated operations for schedule management, run inspection, and explicitly authorized manual retraining. Validate the request and persist its run ID before acknowledging acceptance; do not let client retries create duplicate runs.

component.label: Retraining Control API
component.description: Authenticated boundary for schedule configuration and run-control requests.

properties.purpose: Validate and authorize schedule, run-status, and manual retraining requests with idempotent run creation.

component.highlightReason: Separates operator requests from background execution.

steps.title: Add the identity and policy boundary
steps.content: Authorize schedule changes, approvals, and rollback actions by role. Workload identities used by pipeline stages receive only the permissions needed for their stage; model artifacts and training data are not made public to simplify access.

component.label: Identity & Policy Service
component.description: Role and workload-identity checks for pipeline control and data access.

properties.purpose: Authorize operators and least-privilege pipeline identities for control, data, and release actions.

component.highlightReason: Pipeline automation still needs a clear authorization boundary.

steps.title: Connect the console to the control API
steps.content: The console reads run state and submits authorized schedule or manual-trigger requests. Every mutation carries an idempotency key and actor identity.

connection.label: Schedules & run control
connection.description: Authenticated control requests and run-status responses; mutations carry stable request IDs.

steps.title: Enforce policy before accepting control actions
steps.content: The API checks operator permissions before changing schedules or starting a manual run. Pipeline workers use separate workload identities rather than inheriting an operator token.

connection.label: Identity & authorization
connection.description: Role checks for schedule changes, manual runs, approvals, and rollback operations.

steps.title: Add the trigger and event log
steps.content: Normalize scheduled ticks, approved manual requests, and drift alerts into retraining events. Partition by model or pipeline identity to preserve each model's trigger order; attach an event ID and run ID so duplicate delivery is harmless.

component.label: Retraining Trigger Bus
component.description: Durable event channel for scheduled, manual, and drift-triggered retraining requests.

properties.purpose: Carry idempotent scheduled and event-driven retraining triggers in per-model order.

component.highlightReason: Scheduled and drift-triggered work share one observable, retryable path.

steps.title: Publish accepted control requests
steps.content: After authorization and durable run-record creation, publish a trigger event. If publication fails, leave the request visibly pending or failed and retry with the same run ID; never report a run as accepted when it was lost.

connection.label: Manual & scheduled triggers
connection.description: Authorized requests become durable events with stable run IDs and explicit acceptance state.

steps.title: Add bounded retraining capacity
steps.content: Queue run IDs with per-model deduplication, bounded concurrency, and an explicit priority policy. Backpressure should defer or reject new work visibly instead of exhausting the shared training fleet.

component.label: Retraining Work Queue
component.description: Bounded, retryable dispatch for accepted retraining runs.

properties.purpose: Dispatch idempotent runs with bounded concurrency, backpressure, and visible retry state.

component.highlightReason: Makes load and retry behavior explicit for a four-hour completion target.

steps.title: Dispatch trigger events as work
steps.content: The consumer converts a trigger into one queued run and acknowledges the event only after the run record is durably created. Dead-letter poison events with their run metadata for diagnosis; do not silently drop them.

connection.label: Idempotent run dispatch
connection.description: Durable event-to-run handoff with bounded retries and visible dead-letter handling.

steps.title: Add versioned training-data storage
steps.content: Keep immutable input snapshots and validated dataset manifests outside the run database. A run references a content-addressed manifest so retries and later audits can retrieve the exact same data. The storage provider, encryption key policy, and retention are not specified by the brief.

component.label: Versioned Dataset & Artifact Store
component.description: Durable location for immutable training snapshots, manifests, and candidate artifacts.

properties.purpose: Store immutable dataset snapshots, validated manifests, and model artifacts addressed by run and content hash.

component.highlightReason: Separates large immutable datasets and artifacts from transactional run metadata.

steps.title: Add the validation and preparation workers
steps.content: Workers verify the pinned schema and data contract, completeness, freshness, and basic quality before feature preparation. Compatible schema evolution uses an explicit versioned adapter; incompatible changes quarantine the run with a report instead of silently coercing values.

component.label: Data Validation & Preparation
component.description: Scalable workers that validate pinned inputs and produce reproducible training data.

properties.purpose: Validate schema and data quality, quarantine incompatible inputs, and prepare reproducible training datasets.

component.highlightReason: Puts schema evolution and bad-data prevention before training.

steps.title: Read the exact dataset snapshot
steps.content: The worker resolves the immutable manifest referenced by the run, verifies checksums, and records the resolved version. A newly arrived dataset cannot replace the run's input midway through a retry.

connection.label: Pinned data & schema
connection.description: Immutable, checksum-verified dataset snapshots selected by the run manifest.

steps.title: Run bounded data preparation
steps.content: Workers claim a run with a lease, checkpoint long stages, and renew ownership. A retry resumes from a validated checkpoint or restarts deterministically; stale workers cannot publish a second result for the same run.

connection.label: Leased run jobs
connection.description: Bounded worker dispatch with checkpoints, retry state, and idempotent completion.

steps.title: Add the run and lineage catalog
steps.content: Store run state, input and schema versions, code/configuration digests, gate evidence, actor, and resulting model version as queryable metadata. Keep large datasets and model binaries in object storage, not database rows.

component.label: Run & Lineage Catalog
component.description: Transactional metadata for run state, dataset versions, policy decisions, and model lineage.

properties.purpose: Persist run IDs, dataset and schema versions, code/configuration digests, gate evidence, and model lineage.

component.highlightReason: Makes every retraining outcome reproducible and auditable.

steps.title: Record preparation evidence
steps.content: Persist validation results, quarantines, dataset manifest IDs, and stage timings before the run moves forward. The catalog is the source of run status; the queue is transport, not the lineage record.

connection.label: Run state & validation evidence
connection.description: Transactional run metadata, schema decisions, data-quality results, and stage timings.

steps.title: Define schema compatibility explicitly
steps.content: Keep schema versions and compatibility rules alongside dataset manifests. Additive nullable fields may be accepted only if the feature code declares support; breaking type or semantic changes route to a quarantined dataset and human review. Backfill or dual-read decisions are model-specific and are not assumed here.

steps.title: Add reproducible training and evaluation
steps.content: Train from the pinned dataset and configuration. Evaluate the candidate and incumbent on the same versioned holdout, using the metric and population approved for the model. The brief's greater-than-1% threshold is not meaningful until the owner defines whether it is absolute or relative and which metric it applies to.

component.label: Training & Baseline Evaluation

properties.purpose: Train from pinned inputs and compare candidate with incumbent using the approved metric and evaluation population.

component.highlightReason: Training and baseline comparison are separate from promotion authority.

steps.title: Launch training from validated data
steps.content: Only a run whose input checks passed reaches training. Pin the code, dependencies, feature transformations, parameters, and seeds where applicable; store the resulting model artifact and evaluation report under the run ID.

connection.label: Validated dataset & pinned config
connection.description: Training starts only from a validated, versioned dataset and immutable run configuration.

steps.title: Store the candidate artifact immutably
steps.content: Write the model artifact and its digest to versioned object storage. The registry stores metadata and references the artifact; it does not overwrite the incumbent binary.

connection.label: Candidate artifact & report
connection.description: Immutable candidate model artifact, digest, and evaluation report keyed to the training run.

steps.title: Persist metrics and baseline evidence
steps.content: Record the incumbent version, candidate version, evaluation dataset, metric values, uncertainty, and policy version. A reviewer can reproduce why a run passed or failed without relying on mutable dashboard state.

connection.label: Metrics & run outcome
connection.description: Versioned evaluation evidence and candidate outcome attached to the immutable run record.

steps.title: Make promotion a fail-closed quality gate
steps.content: Promotion requires the approved metric to exceed the incumbent by more than 1% under the agreed comparison method, plus all independent safety and quality checks. Use a statistically appropriate test and sufficient sample size; a noisy point estimate is not proof of improvement. Missing data, inconclusive results, schema incompatibility, or any failed gate keep the candidate in staging and preserve the serving version.

steps.title: Add the versioned model registry
steps.content: Register immutable candidate and incumbent versions with artifact digest, lineage, evaluation evidence, approval state, and rollback target. Maintain separate staged and production aliases so validation cannot move the live pointer accidentally.

component.label: Model Registry & Promotion Gate
component.description: Immutable model versions, lineage, approvals, and environment aliases.

properties.purpose: Track immutable candidate versions, evaluation evidence, approvals, lineage, and staged/production aliases.

component.highlightReason: Separates a trained candidate from an approved production version.

steps.title: Submit candidate evidence for approval
steps.content: The registry accepts a candidate only with the complete run manifest and gate evidence. Failed or incomplete candidates remain non-production versions; approval is an explicit, auditable state transition.

connection.label: Candidate + gate evidence
connection.description: Immutable artifact reference, lineage, baseline comparison, and policy results for promotion review.

steps.title: Compare against the registered incumbent
steps.content: The evaluation stage resolves the incumbent version from the registry and uses the same approved evaluation population for a fair comparison. Do not retrain against a moving baseline during a run.

connection.label: Pinned incumbent version
connection.description: The exact current production version and lineage used for candidate comparison.

steps.title: Keep failed candidates out of production
steps.content: Validation failure leaves the production alias unchanged and records the reason and evidence. If a candidate passes offline checks, continue with shadow or canary evaluation against live traffic before broad promotion; online guardrails and the rollback trigger must be agreed for the model's risk profile.

steps.title: Add zero-downtime model serving
steps.content: Keep the incumbent serving while the candidate is warmed and health-checked. Shift traffic by an atomic version alias or controlled blue-green/canary route; never stop the current model before the replacement is ready.

component.label: Blue-Green Model Serving
component.description: Version-aware endpoint that can stage, promote, and rapidly restore model versions.

properties.purpose: Warm candidate versions and atomically shift traffic while retaining the incumbent for immediate rollback.

component.highlightReason: Makes the zero-downtime swap a serving-plane behavior.

steps.title: Promote only an approved registry version
steps.content: Serving resolves only the approved production alias. The transition preserves the old version until health checks pass and enough evidence exists to complete rollout.

connection.label: Approved production alias
connection.description: Only a gate-passing, authorized model version is eligible for serving traffic.

steps.title: Add production and pipeline observability
steps.content: Track retraining duration, queue age, validation failures, candidate-versus-incumbent metrics, active model version, rollout health, and drift by relevant data segment. Avoid logging raw sensitive training records.

component.label: Pipeline & Model Monitoring
component.description: Operational, quality, drift, and release telemetry for retraining and serving.

properties.purpose: Observe run duration, queue age, data quality, model quality, drift, active version, and release health.

component.highlightReason: Shows whether the four-hour and production-quality targets are met in operation.

steps.title: Measure the active model in production
steps.content: Emit model version, request outcome, latency, and privacy-safe quality signals from serving. Define alert thresholds and minimum sample volumes with the model owner rather than inferring them from the brief.

connection.label: Versioned outcome telemetry
connection.description: Production outcomes and health metrics tagged with the exact served model version.

steps.title: Turn confirmed drift into a controlled trigger
steps.content: Monitoring emits a drift event only after the configured detector's window, sample-size, and severity policy passes. The trigger is deduplicated and enters the same run-ID workflow as scheduled jobs; an alert is not itself permission to promote a model.

connection.label: Qualified drift events
connection.description: Policy-qualified drift signals start an idempotent retraining run, with detector evidence attached.

steps.title: Measure the four-hour completion target
steps.content: Measure end-to-end time from the agreed start boundary through data validation, training, evaluation, and the required approval state. Track queue wait separately from compute time and alert early enough to preserve retry budget. The brief supplies no dataset size or model type, so four-hour feasibility must be demonstrated by representative load tests, not asserted from this diagram.

steps.title: Define the greater-than-one-percent comparison
steps.content: The owner must specify the metric, cohort, absolute-versus-relative interpretation, and significance criterion. Compare candidate and incumbent on a versioned holdout and report uncertainty. If the evidence is inconclusive or the required improvement is not reached, do not promote; retain the incumbent and preserve the full comparison.

steps.title: Make rollback a version-pointer operation
steps.content: Keep the previous artifact warm or quickly loadable and preserve its registry alias. On a failed gate, leave production unchanged; on post-release regression, route traffic back to the last known-good version and open a separately tracked incident. Rollback does not erase the failed model or its lineage.

steps.title: Preserve reproducibility and audit evidence
steps.content: Link every outcome to the trigger, actor, dataset and schema versions, code/container digest, feature transformations, parameters, baseline, gate policy, approvals, artifact digest, deployment state, and rollback event. Retention and privacy rules are not specified; agree them before storing sensitive datasets or metrics.

steps.title: Review the operational failure paths
steps.content: Exercise duplicate triggers, unavailable data, schema breaks, worker loss, exhausted compute, inconclusive evaluation, registry outage, partial canary, and failed rollback. Each path needs an observable terminal state, idempotent recovery, and a rule that protects the currently approved production version.
